content.text: Spring Batch provides several ways to control the flow of steps in a job:

items: Linear Flow of Steps – Steps execute sequentially.
Conditional Flow of Steps – Steps execute based on exit status or conditions.
Split Flow of Steps – Steps execute in parallel (used in scaling scenarios).
Steps execute one after the other in a predefined order.
Achieved using the .next() method of JobBuilder.
firstStep() executes first, followed by secondStep(), then thirdStep().
Simple linear execution, suitable for basic batch processing pipelines.
Step execution can be conditional based on exit status (COMPLETED, FAILED, etc.).
Use .on() and .to() methods to define transitions.
Wildcards () allow less specific matching; exact status strings allow precise control.
This allows handling failures or alternative paths in a batch job.
The RunIdIncrementer ensures a new job instance is created on each run.
A JobExecutionDecider allows programmatic control over job flow.
The decide() method returns a FlowExecutionStatus, which determines the next step.
Spring Batch does not store decider execution metadata in the job repository.
This decider chooses "FN" for morning and "AN" for afternoon.
decider() determines which step runs next based on logic in MyFlowDecider.
Provides dynamic job flow that cannot be achieved with static .next() chaining.
